gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 288 Wh-class picks all deliver about 230 Wh at the AC outlet when measured: SmartZone measured 231 Wh on the EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus, nextpit measured 237 Wh on the Jackery Explorer 300 Plus and The Technology Man measured 231 Wh on the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2. None of those results says either that the Elite 30 V2's AC inverter drew about 19 W at idle with Eco mode off (100% to 19% in 12 hours, The Technology Man).
standout_why: I opened the rival pages. testedwatts.com, powerbencher.com, agentretrievalindex.com, powerstationgearlab.com, volt-vanguard.com and rv.com give only specs or calculated runtimes, and several say outright that they did no testing. Only solarpowerauditor.com has a measured AC figure (Anker SOLIX C300: 232 Wh, 80.6%). It has no measured figure for the RIVER 3 Plus, the Jackery 300 Plus or v2, or the Elite 30 V2. No rival gives a measured AC idle drain or a measured UPS transfer time. Wired.com refused the fetch, so I couldn't check it.
decides: This confirms the RIVER 3 Plus as the pick instead of overturning it. Its 600 W inverter delivered about the same measured AC energy as the 300 W Anker and Jackery units (231 Wh vs 230 and 237 Wh), so the extra output costs no runtime. StorageReview measured its UPS switchover at 9 ms. The shopper should plan on about 230 Wh at the outlet, not 286 to 288 Wh. Anyone looking at the Elite 30 V2 (which Dealectric lists) should turn on Eco mode or switch AC off when idle, because The Technology Man measured about 19 W of AC idle drain.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy (SmartZone)
findings.value: 231 Wh average (228 Wh at 100 W load, 233 Wh at 600 W load), 81% of the 286 Wh rating
findings.source_title: Ecoflow River 3 Plus im Test – kompakt, leistungsstark und leise (smartzone.de)
findings.note: Review by Michael, dated 2025-04-13. It is a German review, and the unit had European 230 V AC output. Same test: USB 220 Wh at a 12 W load and 12 V car socket 250 Wh at 120 W. A full charge from mains took 330 Wh and a little over an hour. Round trip is 231/330 ≈ 70% (my arithmetic). StorageReview's US review reports a 0.43 kWh discharge, which is above the 286 Wh rating and doesn't fit, so I left it out.

findings.label: Measured noise (SmartZone)
findings.value: 30–33 dB(A) at 1 m at maximum load
findings.source_title: Ecoflow River 3 Plus im Test – kompakt, leistungsstark und leise (smartzone.de)

findings.label: Measured UPS transfer time (StorageReview)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus Review: Compact Power Station With 600W Output, UPS Support (StorageReview)
findings.note: Review by Dylan Dougherty, 2025-02-12. Rated at under 10 ms.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy (StorageReview)
findings.value: 210 Wh of 245 Wh rated (≈86%); 270 Wh drawn from the wall to recharge
findings.note: Review by Corinne O'Brien, 2024-10-07. Load was a 300 W fan. Peak AC charge draw measured at 322 W. Round trip is 210/270 ≈ 78% (my arithmetic).

findings.label: Measured usable energy (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.value: 230 Wh of 288 Wh rated (80%); AC recharge 0–100% in 63 min
findings.note: Review by Kenji Mowrey, dated 2026-07-23. The review gives no test load. Tested model is the AC C300 (A1722), sister to the C300X ChatGPT showed. The rival page solarpowerauditor.com has its own measurement of the C300 (232 Wh, 80.6%, at a 300 W load).

findings.label: Measured runtime at 300 W and recharge (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: About 50 min at 300 W (stated as 87% efficiency, ≈250 Wh); wall recharge 0–100% in 1 h 8 min
findings.source_title: Anker C300X Review: Too Good to Be True at Just $199? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: AC version with three 120 V outlets. The page is undated and names no author. The 250 Wh figure is my arithmetic: 300 W × 50/60 h. The review gives no dB figure and only says the unit is 'impressively quiet'.

findings.label: Measured usable energy and round trip (nextpit)
findings.value: 237 Wh out of 288 Wh rated (82%); 327 Wh needed for a full charge; 72% round-trip efficiency; 32 dB in operation
findings.note: Review by Thomas Kern, dated 2023-09-01. It is a German review, and nextpit discloses a cooperation with Jackery. The page doesn't say how the noise was measured. 72% = 237/327, as nextpit states.

findings.label: Measured usable energy (The Technology Man)
findings.value: AC 231 Wh (≈80%), DC 244 Wh (≈85%) of 288 Wh rated; mains recharge 80% in about 40 min and full in 51 min
findings.source_title: This $189 BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 Power Station Is Better Than I Expected (The Technology Man)
findings.note: Review by Gidon, dated 2025-12-23. The load is described only as 'a constant AC load', with no wattage. Turbo mode was used for the recharge.

findings.label: Measured AC idle drain, Eco mode off (The Technology Man)
findings.value: ≈19 W (AC on with no load drained 100% to 19% in 12 h); DC on: ≈11 W (100% to 24% in 20 h)
findings.source_title: This $189 BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 Power Station Is Better Than I Expected (The Technology Man)
findings.note: Watt figures are the reviewer's. Check: 0.81 × 288 Wh ≈ 233 Wh over 12 h ≈ 19.4 W. The reviewer recommends turning Eco mode on.
